newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban accuse Iran, Tajikistan of interference.
newsitem.headline: Taleban accuse Iran, Tajikistan of interference.

text.p: The Taleban authorities on Tuesday accused Iran and Tajikistan of interference in Afghanistan's internal affairs after the two nations' presidents held talks on security with ousted Afghan President Burhanuddin Rabbani.

"The Foreign Ministry of the Islamic State of Afghanistan considers the convening of such meetings, where Afghanistan is discussed without the participation of the central government, as flagrant interference in its internal affairs," a Taleban statement said.
According to reports from Dushanbe, Iranian President Ali Akbar Rafsanjani and Tajik President Imamoli Rakhmanov discussed security issues in a closed-door meeting in the Tajik capital on Sunday.
The Tajik foreign minister said afterwards they had agreed on the need for a peaceful solution to the Afghan conflict.
"They agreed they should get all parties in the conflict to find a peaceful solution", Foreign Minister Talbak Nazarov was quoted as saying.
The Taleban, who control more than two-thirds of Afghanistan, have yet to be recognised as the legitimate authority in Afghanistan by any nation or international body.
A representative of Rabbani's administration, which was driven from Kabul by the Taleban in September last year, still occupies Afghanistan's seat in the United Nations.
The Taleban statement accused the participants of the Dushanbe meeting of fostering tension in the region.

"The Foreign Ministry expresses its strong protest to the Tajik and Iranian authorities and asks them for cooperation instead of interference. Interference creates a tense atmosphere and a lack of trust," said the statement, released in Kabul.

The statement came on a day when representatives of 10 countries in the region, including both Tajikistan and Iran, met at the Economic Cooperation Organisation summit in the Turkmen capital Ashgabat. The Taleban have protested that Rabbani's representative and not their own was invited.
The Taleban have repeatedly accused both Iran and Tajikistan of aiding the opposition alliance in the north of the country. Both countries deny giving military support to the opposition.
Tuesday's Taleban statement reiterated that they had no ambitions outside Afghanistan.

"The Islamic State of Afghanistan under the Taleban has explicitly stated its peaceful intentions towards the international community and has said that it has no intention of interfering in the affairs of other countries," it said.
The Taleban faces an alliance in the northern provinces largely made up of former government forces led by Ahmad Shah Masood and the Uzbek troops of General Abdul Rashid Dostum.
